fact_en: Tendons are the tough, rope-like parts that connect your muscles to your bones.
fact_bis: Ang mga litid mao ang gahi nga bahin nga nagsumpay sa kaunoran ngadto sa bukog.
evidence: 'Buto' names a seed/explosion (and a vulgar term) rather than a bone; the body correctly says tendons join 'kaunoran' to 'bukog'.

fact_en:
How do ants sense danger without ears?

Ants don't have ears like ours — instead, they feel vibrations in the ground through their legs to sense danger.
fact_bis:
Unsaon pagbati sa hulmigas sa katalagman bisan walay dalunggan?

Ang hulmigas walay dalunggan sama sa ato — hinuon, mabati nila ang pag-uyog sa yuta pinaagi sa ilang mga tiil aron mabati ang katalagman.
evidence: 'Langgam Bati Yanig' tells a Cebuano child that BIRDS feel vibrations, while the body is entirely about 'hulmigas' (ants).

fact_en: Folding its leaves costs the makahiya energy, so it only closes them when it really needs to — it doesn't want to waste the energy it needs to grow.
fact_bis: Naggamit og kusog ang makahiya kada mosira kini og dahon, mao nga dili kini basta mosira — dili niini gustong usikan ang kusog nga gikinahanglan aron motubo.
evidence: Last word "Makahiy" is cut off; the card itself contains "Makahiya".

fact_en:
How many more ants are there than people?

About 2.5 million times more! There are way more ants on Earth than there are people.
fact_bis:
Pila ka pilo mas daghan ang hulmigas kaysa tawo?

Mga 2.5 ka milyon ka pilo nga mas daghan! Mas daghan pa ang hulmigas sa kalibotan kaysa tawo.
evidence: The headline number is attached to 'langgam' (birds) instead of 'hulmigas' (ants), which is the word the body uses.

fact_en: Sweat and urine both remove a little water and waste, but they have different main jobs — urine is your body's main blood-cleaner, while sweat is mainly your body's cooler.
fact_bis: Ang singot ug ihi parehong magkuha og tubig ug gamayng hugaw, apan lahi ang ilang trabaho — ang ihi mao ang nag-unang tiglimpyo sa dugo, ang singot mao ang tigpabugnaw sa lawas.
evidence: 'Baul ug Ihi Lain' reads as 'a chest and urine are different'; the card contrasts SINGOT (sweat) with urine, and the body uses 'singot'.

fact_en: Glass is super squishy when hot! While it's still hot and soft, glass can be blown or shaped into many cool and different forms.
fact_bis: Humok kaayo ang salamin kung init! Samtang init pa ug humok, ang salamin mahimong huypan o hulmahon sa lain-laing porma.
evidence: 'Lumot' is MOSS/algae in Cebuano (all 102 corpus body uses are moss or seaweed), so the title reads 'glass hot moss shape' where the card means soft ('humok', used in the body).

fact_en:
Ever wonder why we can bend rubber but not metal?

Rubber is soft and easy to bend! Unlike metal, which is hard and stiff, rubber flexes easily.
fact_bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo ngano nga mabaluktot ang goma pero dili ang puthaw?

Ang goma humok ug sayon baw-ogon! Dili sama sa puthaw nga gahi ug tikig, sayon kini nga baluktuton.
evidence: Leading with 'Lumot' makes the headline 'Moss Rubber Bendable'; the card's whole point is that rubber is HUMOK (soft), the word the body uses.

fact_en:
Why are gold and silver called precious metals?

They are precious because they are rare in the earth, making them very valuable!
fact_bis:
Nganong gitawag nga bililhong metal ang bulawan ug plata?

Tungod kay talagsaon ra sila sa yuta, mao nga taas kaayo ang ilang bili!
evidence: 'Bihag' means CAPTIVE (zero body uses anywhere in the corpus); the title says 'captive expensive metal' where the card means rare — the body correctly says 'talagsaon'.

fact_en:
What precious metal is even rarer than gold?

Platinum is a precious metal rarer than gold, used in expensive jewelry and some machines!
fact_bis:
Unong bililhong metal ang mas talagsaon pa kay sa bulawan?

Ang platino usa ka bililhong metal nga mas talagsaon pa kay sa bulawan, gigamit sa mahal nga alahas ug pipila ka makina!
evidence: 'Platino Bihag kaysa Bulawan' says platinum is more CAPTIVE than gold; the card and body use 'talagsaon' for rare.

fact_en: Magnets ignore plastic, paper, and sand completely! This is exactly why they are perfect for separating iron from those materials.
fact_bis: Ang magneto dili magkabig sa plastik, papel, o balas! Mao nga nindot kaayo kini sa pagtunga sa puthaw gikan niini.
evidence: Last word "Non-Magnet" is cut off; the card itself contains "Non-Magnets".

fact_en: Scientists use chromatography to find out exactly what substances are hiding inside ink, food, or medicine!
fact_bis: Gamiton sa mga siyentista ang chromatography aron mahibaw-an kung unsang mga sangkap ang naa sa tinta, pagkaon, o tambal!
evidence: 'Gamot' again reads as ROOT, so the headline says chromatography of ink and plant roots, while the body correctly says 'tambal' (medicine).

fact_en:
Can a solid be soft?

Yes! A solid can be hard like a rock or soft like a sponge. Both keep their own shape!
fact_bis:
Mahimo bang humok ang solido?

Oo! Ang solido mahimong gahi sama sa bato o humok sama sa espongha. Pareho silang adunay kaugalingong porma!
evidence: 'Lumot' means moss/algae in 102 of 102 Cebuano bodies (soft is always 'humok', e.g. 'Ang lumot sa dagat humok'), so 'Solido Lig-on Lumot Porma' tells a child a solid can be hard or MOSS.
